headline: Democrats flip Congress; final House and Senate counts still firming up
summary: The stories that stayed in the briefing most this week: Democrats flip Congress; final House and Senate counts still firming up; Trump confirms new ‘minor’ US strikes on Iran, says talks are progressing; Canada-U.S. trade talks continue as Democrats vow to repeal tariffs.

top.headline: Democrats flip Congress; final House and Senate counts still firming up
top.what: Networks project Democrats will hold at least 259 House seats and at least 54 Senate seats; the Alaska and Mississippi Senate races are unresolved, with lawyers now involved in a razor-thin Mississippi count.
top.why: In the briefing on 5 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Trump confirms new ‘minor’ US strikes on Iran, says talks are progressing
top.what: President Trump said the U.S. carried out another round of limited strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island while claiming progress in talks to end the war.
top.why: In the briefing on 5 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Canada-U.S. trade talks continue as Democrats vow to repeal tariffs
top.what: Tariffs on Canadian goods remain while talks continue, and the DNC chair says Democrats would move to end them if they win power.
top.why: In the briefing on 5 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Carney government's second budget projects $62.3B deficit with $142B in new spending
top.what: Finance Minister Champagne tabled the budget Thursday: a $62.3-billion deficit for 2026-27 and about $142 billion in new spending over five years.
top.why: In the briefing on 5 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Russian bombing of Ukraine aid centre kills at least 26; Dnipro hit
top.what: Officials say at least 26 people died when Russian bombs hit an aid centre in Komyshuvakha, and separate strikes on Dnipro killed two and injured 20.
top.why: In the briefing on 4 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: With a $1.12-billion budget shortfall looming, Ford rules out a 'new deal' 2.0 for Toronto
top.what: Premier Doug Ford told reporters Ontario will not sign a new funding agreement with Toronto, as the city faces a shortfall of about $1.12 billion in its 2027 budget.
top.why: In the briefing on 4 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Justice Department expands probe into Alaska Senate race 'spoiler' candidate
top.what: The department sent target letters, including to a prominent Democratic attorney, in a criminal probe tied to a second Dan Sullivan on Alaska's Senate ballot.
top.why: In the briefing on 3 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Ontario's deficit swells to $16.9 billion as tariffs delay balanced budget
top.what: Ontario's fall update projects a record $16.9-billion deficit this year and $36 billion over three years.
top.why: In the briefing on 3 of the last 7 days.
